items.title: Muted Distillation: Sealing Reasoning from Teacher Unlocks Token-Efficient Agents
items.title_zh: Muted Distillation：对教师隐藏推理过程，打造更省 token 的 Agent
items.raw_content: Muted Distillation is a variant of on-policy distillation that hides the student's reasoning from the teacher; on OfficeQA Pro and SpreadsheetBench it cuts output tokens per episode by 57% and 53% versus standard OPD, matches OPD accuracy on OfficeQA Pro and improves pass@1 by 4.8 points on SpreadsheetBench.

items.title: RecallWorld: Episodic Memory for Persistent Embodied Video World Models
items.title_zh: RecallWorld：面向持久具身视频世界模型的片段记忆
items.raw_content: RecallWorld is a persistent embodied video world model that reconstructs short multi-view episodes into Scenelets while keeping geometry independent across episodes, using camera-aware ray lifting and coverage-based retrieval; across four datasets it improves revisit PSNR by 2.6 dB on partial revisits and 3.9 dB on full cycles over the strongest evaluated baseline.

items.title: SupportChain: Trace-Calibrated Aggregation of Quote-Grounded Reasoning Chains for Multi-Hop RAG with Small Readers
items.title_zh: SupportChain：面向小模型多跳 RAG 的引用溯源推理链聚合
items.raw_content: SupportChain splits a question into hops, binds each answer to a sentence quoted from a retrieved passage, estimates reliability from execution traces and merges runs by support; with a 9B reader under the HippoRAG 2 protocol it reaches 63.0 F1 on MuSiQue, above the prior best of 59.2 from a 20B reader, and builds no index.

items.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
items.title_zh: 评估基座很重要：多 Agent 服务基座的基准测试
items.raw_content: MASSys is a benchmark that runs the same multi-agent candidate-task pairs across serving substrates and load regimes, recording quality alongside latency, cost and failure evidence; a diagnostic shows the Star workflow falling from first to fourth in mean-latency rank under KV-cache pressure while Chain rises from fourth to first.

items.title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding
items.raw_content:
Authors: Junyi Yang, Zheng Si, Yilin Zhai, Pengpeng Ouyang, Hongxi Wang et al.

Practical highway infrastructure inspection entails progressive diagnostic reasoning from visual perception to maintenance decisions, yet existing benchmarks remain confined to isolated tasks, leaving Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) insufficiently evaluated across sequential inspection stages. Meanwhile, current datasets focus primarily on highway pavement defects, falling short of real-world inspection across diverse infrastructure components such as highway pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage systems. To address these gaps, we formulate the Highway Infrastructure Inspection Progression Chain (HIIP-Chain), spanning Anomaly Detection, Anomaly Recognition, Condition Analysis, and Maintenance Resolution, and introduce HighwayVerse. HighwayVerse comprises 14,143 real-world Ground and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) inspection records spanning 100 and 17 anomaly categories, respectively, with 84,858 expert-reviewed question-answer pairs. We evaluate 12 open-source and closed-source MLLMs using the chained metric Final, which credits a correct maintenance decision only when all preceding diagnostic stages are completed correctly. Results show that although models achieve relatively high accuracy when initially judging whether an anomaly is present, their markedly lower Final scores expose struggles across downstream recognition, analysis, and decision-making. This discrepancy indicates that current MLLMs do not fully comprehend specific highway anomaly patterns beyond superficial initial judgments. Furthermore, we propose LaneRAG, a training-free retrieval-augmented framework that provides hierarchical reference guidance achieving consistent performance improvements across diverse MLLMs. Our dataset, evaluation benchmark, and source code will be publicly released.

items.title: HyperHarness: Learning to Generate Personalized Agent Harnesses from User Histories
items.raw_content:
Authors: Zhaoxuan Tan, Jiachen Zhao, Jingbo Yang, Zheyuan Liu, Chuhan Wang et al.

Personalized LLM agents rely on an agent harness, the surrounding memory and control code, to connect user history with downstream decisions. Existing methods typically employ either a single shared memory workflow across all users, which is efficient to deploy but cannot adapt how evidence is retrieved and interpreted across diverse histories, or per-user harness optimization, which customizes behavior for each user but requires costly repeated candidate evaluation at deployment and suffers from sparse, noisy supervision in raw logs. To address this trade-off, we present HyperHarness, a framework that learns a shared history-to-harness generator to synthesize executable, user-specific retrieval and answer-guidance code directly from user histories. Given a user's permitted history, HyperHarness prompts a construction LLM to write personalized retrieval and guidance functions, while downstream task scores across training users supervise iterative refinements to the shared generator without reference harnesses or answering-model updates. At deployment, the frozen generator constructs a harness for each unseen user in a single pass from history alone, eliminating per-user task-scored search. Across three benchmarks (PersonaMemv3, Mem-PAL, and MemoryCD) and three answering models (Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B, and GPT-5.6-Luna), HyperHarness achieves the highest aggregate score in seven of nine settings and ranks second in the remaining two, improving over the strongest baselines by up to 5.95 points while cutting matched answer-time tokens by 90.32% over long-context prompting. Analyses show that optimization tailors context allocation to each executor, transfers to unseen user clusters, and amortizes adaptation costs.

items.title: LITMUS - Literature Informed Testbed for Mapping Usecases and Synthesizing Risk-Cards
items.raw_content:
Authors: Seshu Tirupathi, Elizabeth M. Daly, Radu Marinescu, Javier Carnerero Cano, Yannis Belkhiter

The proliferation of large language models (LLMs) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in real-world applications has heightened the need for systematic, safety-oriented deployment frameworks. Existing approaches typically prioritize the construction of datasets and risk cards around the LLM and AI architecture itself, yet they provide scant consideration for the specific use-case that drives model selection. This omission is problematic because any practical AI deployment begins with a detailed use-case description that informs the assessment of contextual hazards. In this paper, we introduce a structured pipeline that, given a use-case, automatically produces a tailored dataset and an accompanying risk card. The process ensures that identified risks are tightly coupled to the use-case, and it offers traceable evidence from peer-reviewed literature to substantiate each risk to use-case relationship. Prior claim-verification methods (FActScore, FactReasoner) have been validated for factual claims. Risk-relevance is a hypothetical claim about possible harm, and whether evidence retrieval can meaningfully assess such claims remains untested. Literature-Informed Testbed for Mapping Use-cases and Synthesizing (LITMUS) risk cards are the first systematic attempt to characterize this adaptation. We evaluated the pipeline using the MIT Risk Taxonomy and achieved a 0.91 F1-score with a list of 320 samples from the benchmark risk dataset that was considered. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in generating robust, evidence-based risk assessments for LLM deployments.

items.title: Thakaa at AlexandriaX-2026: Who Gets the Final Say? Assigning Output Authority in Dialectal Arabic Machine Translation and Error Detection
items.raw_content:
Authors: Meshal Alamr, Maryam Altuwaijri, Hassan Alqaeri, Abdullah Aldahlawi

We report first-place systems for all four evaluated AlexandriaX-2026 settings: both English-to-dialect translation tracks, cross-dialect translation, and translation-error detection. In unconstrained translation, our minimum Bayes risk (MBR) selection restricts output authority: four local systems can supply the translation, while seven additional systems contribute only reference evidence. Candidate-constrained MBR beats the strongest complete candidate in all 13 dialects and gains 1.2554 macro spBLEU overall, reaching 33.4891. It also surpasses a retrospective oracle selecting the best whole candidate system per dialect. In the constrained track, country-routed LoRA adapters over a shared NileChat-3B-Base backbone incorporate the released Libyan and Sudanese supervision absent from the training and development splits, raising macro spBLEU from 29.5969 to 30.4233. Post-evaluation, a single adapter trained on all released Alexandria data reaches 30.4733 macro spBLEU; averaging model weights across three training seeds raises this to 30.9726 while retaining one model for inference. For cross-dialect translation, nonparallel target-dialect retrieval guides deliberation, raising Gemma-4-31B-IT without fine-tuning from 24.6898 to 28.4011 spBLEU. For translation-error detection, GPT-5.5 proposes semantic error regions, while MARBERTv2 controls their character boundaries and corroborates additional spans, raising Overall from 0.4691 to 0.4982.

items.title: Thakaa at StanceEval-2026: Inference-Time Target Grounding for Arabic Stance Detection
items.raw_content:
Authors: Meshal Alamr, Hassan Alqaeri, Abdullah Aldahlawi

StanceEval-2026 tests Arabic stance classification under target shift, with evaluation targets absent from the labelled task data. We test two ways to supply target information at inference time. For Track 1, we retrieve eight labelled Women Driving demonstrations from the external ArabicStanceX corpus and score the three label tokens with Gemma-4-31B-IT. For the unseen-target track, we prepend cached target context prompted to be factual and non-evaluative, then fuse label predictions and label-token scores from multiple LLMs, with final assignments constrained by published class totals. The systems obtain 85.22 and 91.78 Favg2 on Tracks 1 and 2, ranking sixth and fourth in the final standings. On held-out ArabicStanceX tweets, direct prompting scores 79.45 Favg2; eight random Women Driving demonstrations raise it to 84.78, and similarity retrieval reaches 89.04. Across three target-held-out Mawqif evaluations, a fixed target card raises Gemma-4-31B-IT from 86.54 to 86.93, whereas QLoRA lowers Gemma-4-12B-IT from 84.43 to 83.77. In these separate public evaluations, same-target demonstrations and retrieval improve performance, factual target context provides small, target-dependent gains, and the tested source-only adapter does not improve.

items.title: AgriManager: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-RL Generalization in Agricultural Management
items.raw_content:
Authors: Chi Gui, Junwen Zheng, Ritwik Nigam, Qianlan Yang, Meagan Lang et al.

Agricultural management is heterogeneous along two axes. The first is distributional shift within a fixed task interface: weather, crops, and prices vary across years and locations while sensors, actions, and objective stay fixed. The second is structural shift across interfaces: different farms expose different observed variables, available actions, and management objectives. We formalize the second axis as schema shift: variation in the policy-facing schema $Σ= (Σ_O, Σ_A, Σ_R)$ between training and deployment. We test whether LLM-RL generalizes across both axes with AgriManager, to our knowledge the first framework that trains LLM policies with RL across multiple process-based crop simulators, unifying DSSAT, WOFOST, and Cycles. We design a three-tier generalization ladder: Tier 1 within-schema distributional shift, Tier 2 single-axis schema shift along $Σ_O / Σ_A / Σ_R$, Tier 3 compositional schema shift across simulators, all scored on a frozen held-out test suite with three training seeds per method. Within fixed schemas, Qwen3-4B trained by RL with explicit reasoning exceeds neural-network PPO trained with the same interaction budget; without reasoning, training stalls near no-action where the reward penalizes input use. Under single-axis schema shift, $Σ_O$ transfer needs decision-critical state, $Σ_A$ results are consistent with joint action-menu coverage, and with reasoning a policy trained on yield alone transfers to unseen objectives. Under compositional schema shift, single-source training mostly hurts zero-shot transfer across simulators, and a unified policy trained only on other combinations of the same components recovers about 86% of the gain of a specialist trained on the target combination on DSSAT and stays below the specialists on the WOFOST and Cycles profit targets. Project page: https://agrimanager-framework.github.io

items.title: CLASP: Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling for Zero-Shot OOD Detection using Vision-Language Models
items.raw_content:
Authors: Saahil Islam, Adarsh Bhandary Panambur, Teodora Spasojevic, Eduardo Castaneda, Andreas Maier

Vision-language models (VLMs) enable zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in medical imaging, yet existing approaches often rely on final-layer confidence or entropy-based layer selection, potentially missing complementary information. We show that low in-distribution (ID) confidence entropy does not reliably predict OOD discrimination. We introduce CLASP (Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling), an ID-only framework that jointly models layer--prompt responses and visual features. CLASP ranks visual encoder layers using Gaussian conditional mutual information and selects a compact subset through anchored spectral selection, without fixing the number of layers. It then combines the selected layer--prompt profiles with PCA-compressed visual embeddings and fits a single shrinkage-regularized Gaussian. OOD scores are computed using squared Mahalanobis distance, without fine-tuning, OOD training data, or test-time adaptation. Across histopathology, chest X-ray, and brain MRI benchmarks with UniMedCLIP and BioMedCLIP, CLASP performs strongly under varied distribution shifts. On MIDOG near-OOD, it achieves 87.54% AUROC with UniMedCLIP, outperforming confidence-based baselines; with BioMedCLIP, it remains competitive but trails visual-only Mahalanobis modeling. Ablations highlight the value of layer--prompt interactions and cross-feature dependencies, while exposing shift-dependent contributions and limitations under semantic shifts.

items.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings
items.raw_content:
Authors: Disha Sheshanarayana, Tanishka Magar

The deployment of large language models in operational settings demands evaluation of judgment under institutional constraint. We introduce DiscernBench, a benchmark for evaluating cooperative discernment: the ability of an agent to determine whether to comply with, refuse, or escalate a request in an institutional setting. DiscernBench comprises scenarios derived from real-world incident reports across domains such as aviation, law enforcement, and emergency management. We evaluate eight LLMs across three decision-making configurations and analyze both final decisions and the intermediate judgments produced during multi-agent deliberation. Under disagreement, Final Responders exhibit model- and role-dependent aggregation patterns in which a lone specialist recommendation can disproportionately influence the collective decision, a phenomenon we term Minority-Signal Override. Role-specialized multi-agent deliberation raises average over-escalation from 3.79% under direct single-agent judgment to 28.27%, with the direction and magnitude of minority-signal influence varying substantially across models and specialist roles. These results reveal distinct collective decision behaviors that are not captured by final-answer accuracy alone. Trustworthy multi-agent systems therefore require evaluating not only individual specialist reasoning, but also how conflicting judgments are transformed into collective decisions. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Disha1001/DiscernBench.

items.title: From Reward Engineering to Data-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Effective Agentic Visual Tool Use
items.title_zh: 从奖励工程到数据中心强化学习：提升 Agent 的视觉工具使用
items.raw_content: AOVO is a data-centric framework that teaches multimodal LLMs when to invoke visual tools through perception attribution and policy-adaptive data sampling, without tool-specific rewards; it counterfactually probes reasoning states to find observation-sensitive questions and reallocates training toward them, improving over competitive tool-use models across visual perception and reasoning benchmarks.

items.title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
items.title_zh: Open Vision Banana：在 RGB 空间通过生成实现统一视觉感知的开源框架
items.raw_content: Open Vision Banana adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into one instruction-driven model for metric depth, semantic, instance and referring segmentation with a single shared low-rank adapter and public data; the study finds geometry is learned early but absolute scale is not, and that depth and 2D segmentation compete for the shared adapter, with code, contracts, training data and evaluation outputs released.

items.title: BIRD-Persona: A Persona-Aware Benchmark for SQL and pandas Analytics Code Generation
items.title_zh: BIRD-Persona：面向 SQL 与 pandas 分析代码生成的人物画像感知基准
items.raw_content: BIRD-Persona extends BIRD-Python with novice and expert rewrites, schema variants and task-structure annotations for tasks with matched SQL and pandas ground truth; across 1,534 tasks, nine models and 245,592 evaluations, SQL outperforms pandas for eight of nine systems, and expert, schema-explicit prompts help both paradigms but help SQL more.

items.title: WorldWeave: Rethinking Embodied Navigation through Cross-Task World Modeling
items.title_zh: WorldWeave：以跨任务世界建模重构具身导航
items.raw_content: WorldWeave is a cross-task world model for mobile embodied tasks that learns latent actions from observed state changes via inverse-forward dynamics, sharing transition representations across vision-and-language navigation and embodied visual tracking and feeding future-state predictions into task-specific decision making; experiments show consistent gains over specialized baselines.

items.title: Tool-to-Self: Internalizing Visual Tool Capabilities via Scaffolded Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: Tool-to-Self：通过脚手架式强化学习内化视觉工具能力
items.raw_content: Tool-to-Self is a tool-scaffolded reinforcement learning framework that treats external visual tools as temporary training scaffolds, cold-starting tool use and observation prediction before progressively annealing tool execution on a per-tool basis; it improves over explicit tool-use and implicit zooming models across benchmarks while enabling tool-free inference with lower latency.

items.title: EL4CTEO/fast-anything
items.title_zh: fast-anything：只重写最慢的 5%，用编码 Agent 把热点函数移植到 Rust
items.raw_content: A Rust tool that argues against rewriting whole projects in Rust, instead profiling Python, Node or Ruby apps, porting the hot functions with a coding agent and proving they behave the same.

items.title: w01fb0ss/PiBot
items.title_zh: PiBot：本地优先的开源桌面 AI Agent 团队
items.raw_content: PiBot is an open-source, local-first AI agent team for the desktop with multi-agent group chats, computer use, browser access, MCP, routines and approvals, available on macOS, Windows, Linux and Android and built on pi.
